Title: Design of multi-mode intelligent system architecture for surface defect detection of steel based on cloud technology
Text:
Design of multi-mode intelligent 
system architecture for surface 
defect detection of steel based on 
cloud technology
Fei Ren1,2,3,8, LiBing Xu4,8, Jiajie Fei3, John Paul Q. Tomas1, HongSheng Li3 & 
Bonifacio T. Doma Jr.5,6,7
This research establishes an advanced cloud-native multimodal intelligent system architecture 
dedicated to automated detection and real-time monitoring of steel surface defects. The architecture 
ingeniously integrates the advantages of edge computing, cloud computing, and mobile computing 
technologies, achieving efficient processing and precise analysis of industrial big data through 
advanced deep learning algorithms. The main innovative contributions of this research include: 
(1) Optimized deployment of improved YOLOv5-based algorithm systems, including YOLOv5-
efficient net and YOLOv5-mobile net series lightweight models, which significantly enhance defect 
recognition capabilities in complex industrial environments; (2) Meticulously designed microservice 
architecture and distributed message queue system, realizing high availability and dynamic scalability; 
(3) Pioneering construction of a multi-dimensional intelligent result distribution ecosystem, 
encompassing cross-platform services (WeChat, email), real-time push notifications (iMessage), and 
mobile application alerts (Android applications), ensuring seamless and timely delivery of detection 
results to different end users. In rigorous evaluations on a large-scale self-built steel defect dataset, 
the system demonstrates good performance across key metrics including detection accuracy, recall 
rate, and processing speed. Practical deployment has validated the system’s high reliability and 
robust adaptability in industrial production environments. This research not only provides a feasible 
technical solution for the intelligent transformation of the steel industry but also establishes a forward-
looking technical paradigm for intelligent manufacturing in the context of Industry 4.0, laying a solid 
foundation for achieving unmanned, high-quality modern industrial production.
Keywords  Steel surface defect detection, Cloud-native technology, Multimodal intelligent system 
architecture, Deep learning algorithms, Real-time monitoring
In the modern steel production process, ensuring product quality meets high standards is crucial. Surface defect 
detection in steel, as a key aspect of quality control, traditionally relies on manual visual inspection. However, 
this method is not only inefficient but also susceptible to subjective judgments and environmental factors. 
With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, especially the applications of deep learning1–3 
and cloud technology, efficient and accurate automated detection systems[4–6] have become a research focus. 
Scholars both domestically and internationally have conducted relevant studies.
Sung-suk Choi et al.7 developed a defect detection system based on CCD cameras and computers. The 
system utilizes CCD cameras to capture real-time images for inspection, which are then processed using 
image processing algorithms such as Gaussian filtering and the Canny operator to detect defects. Compared 
to traditional manual inspection methods, this system demonstrates higher efficiency and easier scalability. 
However, its detection accuracy, achieved solely through image processing algorithms, is limited. This limitation

Wang et al.8 designed a hub defect detection system based on image processing technology. They employed 
image preprocessing methods to enhance image features, generating a training dataset used to train a neural 
network for defect detection. The system detects surface defects on hubs using the trained model and displays 
real-time detection results on a host computer. This system performs well in defect detection tasks by integrating 
image processing and neural networks. However, its limitation lies in displaying detection results solely on the 
host computer, necessitating additional means for result dissemination. Li et al.9 addressed the issue of smoke 
and toxic gas generation during arc welding processes by proposing a defect detection system based on robot 
vision. This system employs arc welding robots equipped with visual sensors to replace manual image capture 
and utilizes deep learning combined with edge-cloud computing technologies for defect detection. Additionally, 
it employs Internet of Things (IoT) and virtual simulation technologies for monitoring the entire detection 
system. This system effectively accomplishes defect detection tasks, achieving higher efficiency and speed. Tang 
et al.10 proposed a privacy-preserving classification scheme to address data upload privacy concerns. The scheme 
encrypts original steel images and designs a convolutional neural network capable of processing encrypted 
images for classification. By incorporating distributed computing and edge-cloud architectures, the scheme 
enhances detection speed effectively. Experimental results demonstrate the scheme’s ability to achieve efficient 
image classification while ensuring the privacy of the classification process.
Ling Xiao et al.11 proposed a Convolutional Neural Network (H-CNN) model based on instance level 
features for surface defect detection. This model generates defect masks by extracting features from different 
convolutional layers, and first generates candidate regions. Then, it uses a fully convolutional neural network to 
extract convolutional features at different levels and detect instance level defects. This model has been applied to 
oil stain detection in the Freight Train Detection System (FTDS), and experimental results show that H-CNN 
can effectively identify and generate defect masks. Weishan Zhang et al.12 proposed a distributed embedded 
platform based on NVIDIA Jetson TX1, which utilizes deep learning technology for real-time video processing. 
This platform aims to implement complex deep learning algorithms on low-power devices. Compared with 
high-end GPUs such as NVIDIA TITAN X, this platform significantly reduces power consumption at the same 
processing speed, at the same time, it has good scalability and fault tolerance, and is suitable for intelligent 
mobile devices such as unmanned aerial vehicles or autonomous vehicle.
Han et al.13 introduced an intelligent detection system for membrane fouling in membrane bioreactors 
(MBR), aimed at predicting membrane permeability, evaluating MBR performance, and reducing fouling. The 
system is based on recursive fuzzy neural networks and combines the least squares method to develop a new 
platform that connects sensors and software to facilitate the execution of complex algorithms. The experimental 
results show that the system can monitor membrane permeability in real-time and detect fouling early, optimize 
MBR operation, and improve wastewater treatment efficiency. Liu et al.14 studied a paper based triboelectric 
nanogenerator (BP-TENG) technology and integrated machine learning techniques, A multifunctional and 
multi scenario intelligent detection system has been implemented, capable of real-time handwriting to speech 
conversion, personalized jump prediction, and smart home automation, with a recognition accuracy rate of up 
to 99.8%. The system has high precision, environmental sustainability, and cost-effectiveness, making it suitable 
for applications in communication security, sports and health monitoring, and intelligent building management, 
thereby enhancing the potential of frictional electric sensing technology in intelligent systems.
In this research, ‘multimodal’ (multi-mode) carries a dual meaning: it refers to the system’s support for 
multiple data input modalities, including images, video streams, and real-time camera acquisition, enabling 
flexible adaptation to various detection scenarios; it also indicates the system’s implementation of multiple result 
output modalities, delivering detection results to users across different platforms through various channels 
such as WeChat, email, iMessage, and Android application notifications. This multimodal design demonstrates 
significant adaptability and practicality in diverse industrial environments, effectively meeting the complex 
requirements for defect detection in modern steel production processes.
This research pioneered the construction of a cloud-native multimodal intelligent system architecture, 
bringing breakthrough innovations to the field of steel surface defect detection: meticulously optimizing a series 
of advanced lightweight detection algorithms based on YOLOv5, significantly enhancing intelligent recognition 
capabilities in edge computing environments; elegantly implementing the integration of PyQt framework with 
deep learning algorithms, creating a multidimensional data input ecosystem; adopting microservice architecture 
and cloud technologies with foresight, building a distributed intelligent platform with exceptional resilience 
and scalability; innovatively designing a local-cloud-mobile collaborative push mechanism, achieving seamless 
cross-platform delivery of detection results; and confirming the system’s outstanding reliability and adaptability 
through the validation in industrial environments. The “multimodal” concept in this research is manifested both 
in the diversified data acquisition channels and in the comprehensive result distribution strategies, effectively 
addressing the complex and variable defect detection requirements in modern steel production. It establishes 
a forward-looking technical paradigm for the intelligent transformation of the steel industry, promoting 
innovative development of intelligent manufacturing in the Industry 4.0 era.
Application of cloud technology
In this section, a comprehensive review of the current state of research on cloud technology applications in the 
industrial field is presented, with particular focus on the development of cloud technology architectures in the 
context of Industry 4.0.The Fourth Industrial Revolution elevated manufacturing to a new level by introducing 
intelligent, scalable, flexible, modular, and customized mass production technologies. In order to meet the 
requirements of Industry 4.0, production lines or machines need to be integrated at the management level to 
create and optimize customer-oriented production while maintaining good performance. Despite the significant 
effectiveness demonstrated by industrial cloud technology in practice, as its usage continues to deepen, some core

to finished product delivery15,16. This architecture leverages computing resources, storage, and network services 
in cloud environments to perform real-time data analysis and optimize related business processes. Additionally, 
through the deployment of encryption transmission, secure protocols, and enhanced reliability measures, this 
architecture ensures the security of data transmission and the reliability of information17,18. Such comprehensive 
solutions provide a solid technological foundation for the intelligent upgrading of the manufacturing industry.
The enterprise’s internal information technology systems, hardware facilities, and various functions have 
fully transitioned to a service-oriented model and deployed on top of industrial cloud platforms. Within the 
architecture of the industrial cloud platform, services encompass integrated production control, industrial 
collaboration, and full lifecycle management of equipment assets from procurement to decommissioning. These 
services include comprehensive business support such as intelligent device control, process control, production 
execution systems, enterprise resource planning, and management and analysis of industrial big data.
As more and more small and medium-sized enterprises adopt public cloud software services, some 
companies even use Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) to replace self-built information systems. Meanwhile, 
cloud application services specifically tailored for the industrial sector have also been developed by third-party 
vendors19. These trends necessitate that enterprise IT systems be built on a hybrid cloud architecture. As depicted 
in Fig. 2, this figure illustrates the modern enterprise’s cloud-based IT architecture. Figure 2 highlights the tight 
integration between public cloud service providers and private cloud resource pools, offering customized cloud 
computing solutions for enterprises of all sizes. This architecture not only enhances the flexibility and innovation 
capabilities of enterprises but also opens new possibilities for the widespread adoption and application of 
information technology in various fields.
Multi-mode full-process steel surface defect detection technology based on local-
cloud
Surface defect detection at local nodes: combining YOLO with PyQ
This paper integrates the YOLO object detection algorithm with the PyQt framework. A model with satisfactory 
performance after training is utilized, and the system framework is depicted in Fig. 3. The user interface is 
designed and implemented under the PyQt framework, integrating the YOLO model into the GUI. A video 
stream/image processing module is created in this study, initiating video stream/image processing and 
implementing user interaction functionalities, including responding to user operations20–23. This method 
effectively achieves efficient and accurate steel surface defect detection by combining the YOLO object detection 
algorithm with the PyQt framework. It offers significant advantages such as real-time capability, accuracy, user-
friendliness, integrability, automation, and adaptability.
The seamless integration of PyQt framework with YOLO in this research achieves an efficient information 
transmission mechanism. This mechanism processes user interaction events through a signal-slot design 
pattern, transferring captured image data to the YOLO model via multi-threading while avoiding UI thread 
blocking. The system employs asynchronous processing methods and local caching strategies, ensuring stability 
under various network conditions. Through data serialization in JSON format, combined with REST API design, 
efficient communication between local nodes and cloud services is realized. Detection results are intuitively

cloud data push: utilizing Qiniu cloud service
This paper adopts Qiniu Cloud technology to realize cloud data storage, transfer, and push. Qiniu Cloud enables 
functionalities including object storage, file storage, and CDN acceleration, offering innovative and flexible 
combinations for industrial scenarios based on massive data. The specific architecture of cloud data processing

This paper utilizes Qiniu Cloud’s object storage service to store a large amount of deep learning-detected steel 
surface defect results, ensuring the security and reliability of the data. Upon receiving data, CDN acceleration 
service is employed to achieve high-speed data push and distribution, enabling rapid transmission and access of 
data globally, thereby providing users with a fast and stable data access experience.
Steel surface defect multi-mode full-process detection based on meow reminder
Meow Reminder is a WeChat public account that provides intelligent reminder services, assisting users in 
receiving real-time information through its push function. The integrated steel surface defect multi-mode full-
process detection system, incorporating human-computer interaction technology and deep learning algorithms, 
can promptly identify and classify defects during the production process by monitoring and analyzing images 
of the steel surface in real time. The WeChat server data processing flowchart is depicted in Fig. 5. Leveraging 
Meow Reminder’s push function and cloud technology, this system achieves real-time transmission of defect 
information, significantly enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of steel surface quality control. The system’s 
design takes into account its flexible adaptability, enabling continuous optimization with advancements in 
production technology and changes in market demand, further reducing scrap rates and saving production 
costs.

Experimental design and implementation
Design and implementation of steel surface defect detection interface using PyQt
This paper utilizes the PyQt framework to design and implement a subsystem for steel surface defect detection. 
By integrating human-computer interaction technology and deep learning algorithms, it provides users with an 
intuitive and user-friendly operating environment for real-time detection and analysis of steel surface defects. 
The specific subsystem is illustrated in Fig. 9.
As shown in Fig. 9, we can select the input image, video, or camera in the upper right corner of the detection 
interface. At the center of the detection interface, the object to be detected and the detection results of the object 
can be displayed, including the category, confidence level, and location of the defect. In the bottom right corner 
of the detection interface, you can also see that you can save and exit the detected results.
 Steel surface defect dataset detection based on deep learning
Data serves as the foundation for artificial intelligence and machine learning models, directly impacting the 
training effectiveness and prediction accuracy of models. This study is based on the steel surface defect dataset 
from Northeastern University for training purposes24. Additionally, to ensure the effectiveness and practicality 
of the system, this study focuses on real-world datasets. A specialized company was commissioned to collect 
and create the steel surface defect dataset, guaranteeing that the system can make effective predictions in real 
production environments. Through this specialized data collection and creation process, this study obtained a 
representative steel surface defect dataset, which includes six types of defects: crazing, inclusion, patches, pitted 
surface, rolled-in scale, and scratches, totaling 472 defects.

Steel surface defect detection based on deep learning
The core breakthrough in this research regarding the YOLOv5 model architecture lies in the strategic 
reconstruction of the backbone network. This paper meticulously designs alternatives based on EfficientNet-B1/
B2 and MobileNet series, successfully replacing the original CSPDarknet53 backbone network structure of 
YOLOv5. EfficientNet achieves a balance between feature expression capability and computational efficiency 
through its compound uniform scaling mechanism and optimized convolutional block design; the MobileNet 
series, with its innovative depth-wise separable convolution and inverted residual structure, significantly 
reduces parameter count and floating-point operations while maintaining feature extraction capabilities. This 
backbone network reconstruction not only optimizes the information flow transmission efficiency of the Feature 
Pyramid Network (FPN) but also enhances the model’s sensitivity to minute defects and textural features on steel 
surfaces. Quantitative evaluation demonstrates that this architectural innovation achieves a trade-off between 
computational complexity and detection performance in the field of steel surface defect detection, providing 
an efficient and reliable algorithmic foundation for industrial-grade edge intelligence applications. Regarding 
the availability of the self-built large-scale steel defect dataset, this dataset was collected and annotated by 
professional companies and is currently only available for internal research use under confidentiality agreements. 
However, researchers can obtain usage permissions after review by contacting the corresponding author, or use 
the Northeastern University open-source dataset mentioned in this paper for comparative experiments.
To improve the accuracy and efficiency of detection, this study uses a deep learning approach, specifically 
employing the improved YOLOv5 algorithm for steel surface defect detection. Algorithms such as YOLOv5, 
YOLOv5-efficient net-b1-YOLOv5-efficient net-b8, YOLOv5-mobile net-large, and YOLOv5-mobile net-small25 
were trained on the dataset collected by the team of Song Kechen from Northeastern University. Additionally,

 Implementation of local-cloud-mobile result push
The implementation of the local-cloud-mobile result push system for steel surface defect detection, based on 
deep learning, consists of three main components: the local end, the cloud server, and the mobile end. The local 
end is responsible for collecting and detecting data and then sending it to the cloud server. The cloud server 
processes and analyzes the data and then pushes the results to the mobile end. The Android end is configured 
with a Huawei Honor V8 phone featuring a Hisilicon Kirin 955 series CPU, 128GB ROM, and an Android 8.0.0 
system. The Apple end is configured with an iPhone 12, equipped with an Apple A14 CPU, 128GB ROM, and 
IOS 17.3.1 system. Experimental results are illustrated in Table 1.
The experiments demonstrate that this study has successfully designed and implemented a multi-module 
intelligent system integrating local, cloud, and mobile terminals. This system, based on improved deep learning 
technology, is capable of adapting to the steel surface defect detection requirements in various scenarios. By 
leveraging advanced artificial intelligence and cloud technology, the system achieves high-speed transmission 
and processing of real-time data. The technical framework and system of this study possess robust capabilities 
to efficiently push detection results to various user groups. Users, regardless of whether they are using Android 
or iOS operating systems, can receive detection results through multiple channels such as WeChat and email. 
For iOS users, the system can also send iMessage reminders, while for Android users, real-time reminders can 
be received through dedicated applications. This design significantly enhances the real-time nature of steel 
detection results and the convenience of user reception, providing users with a more efficient and personalized 
service experience.
Conclusion
This study proposes and implements a multi-modal intelligent system architecture based on cloud-native 
technology for automatic detection and monitoring of steel surface defects. The system integrates edge 
computing, cloud computing, and mobile computing technologies to achieve efficient processing and analysis of 
industrial big data. The main innovations and achievements of the research are as follows:
	1.	 Detection algorithm optimization: Based on the improved YOLOv5 algorithm, various lightweight models 
were introduced, significantly enhancing detection performance in complex industrial environments.
	2.	 System architecture innovation: Adopting microservice architecture and distributed message queues, the 
system achieved high availability and scalability. In deployment tests of different scales, the system consist­
ently demonstrated stable performance and good elasticity.
	3.	 Multi-dimensional result distribution mechanism: Developed diverse result distribution channels including 
cross-platform services, real-time push notifications, and mobile application alerts, ensuring timely delivery 
of detection results.

Experimental results show that on a self-built large-scale steel defect dataset, this system outperforms existing 
methods in key indicators such as detection accuracy, recall rate, and processing speed. Long-term deployment 
results further confirm the system’s reliability and scalability in actual production environments.
However, this study still has some limitations. As the scale and complexity of datasets increase, the system’s 
generalization ability may face challenges.With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, 
the following trends may emerge in the field of intelligent surface defect detection: (1) The application of self-
supervised learning and few-shot learning methods to reduce dependence on large amounts of annotated data; 
(2) The development of multimodal fusion technologies, such as combining visual, acoustic, and thermal imaging 
data to provide more comprehensive defect information; (3) The integration of explainable AI technologies to 
make detection results more interpretable and increase industrial experts’ trust in the system; (4) The maturation 
of edge AI technologies, enabling online detection with lower latency and higher energy efficiency; (5) The deep 
integration of digital twin technology with defect detection, facilitating a transition from detection to prediction 
and supporting preventive maintenance. These developments will further advance the level of intelligent 
manufacturing in the steel industry, achieving production goals of higher quality and lower costs.
In conclusion, this study provides an implementable solution for the intelligent transformation of the steel 
industry, while also offering a valuable technical paradigm for intelligent manufacturing in the context of Industry 
4.0. Through continuous optimization and innovation, we believe that this multi-modal intelligent system will 
play an important role in promoting the digital transformation of manufacturing and improving product quality, 
making positive contributions to increasing production efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing enterprise 
competitiveness.
